the maximum entropy method can be generalized to the multistep case and that the resulting extension maximizes the minimum mean-square prediction error.

the problem of extending a finite sequence of correlations so as to maximize the multistep prediction error.
the problem of extending a finite set of autocorrelations so that the power spectrum associated with the resulting sequence is nonnegative everywhere.
the problem of extending finite sequences of autocorrelations of discrete-time stochastic processes in a way that maximizes the minimum mean-square prediction error.

the maximum entropy spectrum extension method is a very general technique for obtaining admissible extensions of finite sequences of autocorrelations that maximize the minimum prediction error.

the maximum entropy extension is not the only extension that maximizes the minimum mean-square-error associated with k-step predictors, and the solution that is obtained from the proposed method is the one that maximizes the error associated with the k-step predictor that minimizes the maximum error among all k-step predictors.
